summary: The v1 helper's fee-matching primitives (fee_rule_matches/applicable_fee_ids/average_fee_across_rules) generalise well for lookup and average-across-rules questions, and the fraud-rate and manual-undefined-concept ground rules are solid, generic fixes. The champion is brittle in two places verified against real data this cycle: best_matching_fee's 'most-specific-rule-wins' resolution is the wrong model for 'what would this merchant currently pay under rule X' / delta questions (task 1871), and the fee-matching function signatures (mcc vs merchant_category_code, required-kwarg-heavy applicable_fee_ids) repeatedly cost the agent a wasted turn-and-retry across several passing tasks, which is a turn-budget risk given task 2697 already failed on max_turns.
notes: VERIFIED ROOT CAUSE for task 1871 (still failing): I recomputed the Jan-2023 Belles_cookbook_store / fee-ID-384 delta two ways. Using helper.best_matching_fee (the agent's approach, and the 'correct' specificity-based pick) selects only 8 of the 12 transactions that satisfy rule 384's own card_scheme/is_credit/aci fields, giving -0.80054 (the agent's wrong answer). Using a plain fee_rule_matches(rule_384, **txn_fields) filter over ALL transactions whose fields satisfy rule 384 — with NO specificity tie-break against other matching rules — selects 12 transactions and gives -0.9481029999999999, which matches gold -0.94810300000017 to float precision. So for 'what delta would a merchant pay if fee ID=X changed' questions, the gold methodology treats rule X as applying to every transaction matching X's own fields, not just the transactions for which X is the single most-specific matching rule. best_matching_fee's docstring claim ('the single fee rule that would actually be charged') is not what these delta questions want. Recommend either adding a dedicated helper (e.g. `fee_delta_for_rule(payments_subset, fees, rule_id, new_fixed=None, new_rate=None)` built on the simple-filter semantics) or an explicit system.md rule telling the agent: for 'delta if fee ID=X changed' questions, select transactions via fee_rule_matches(rule_X, **txn_fields) directly, not best_matching_fee.

This template has 20 siblings (other merchants/months/fee IDs) all sharing the exact same bug, since the underlying tool (best_matching_fee) is what the ground rules currently steer agents toward. Fixing this is high-leverage — one helper/system.md change likely converts ~20 leaderboard failures to passes.

Before reusing best_matching_fee for any other question type, verify its specificity semantics against at least one more example the same way I did for 1871 — do not assume it's correct just because it's plausible; it was already flagged in cycle 1 as 'not tuned to this task's exact number' for task 2697, which is consistent with it encoding the wrong resolution rule rather than merely an off-by-one.

Recurring friction (not yet a correctness bug, but a turn-budget risk): agents guessed wrong keyword names for the fee-matching functions in at least 2 of 5 hard tasks that used them (task 1305: passed `merchant_category_code=` to average_fee_across_rules/fee_rule_matches, which only accepts `mcc=`, raising TypeError; task 1464: called applicable_fee_ids with an `aci=` kwarg it doesn't accept, and with `account_type='R'` alone since it's also missing the required `transactions`/`mcc`/`capture_delay`/`monthly_fraud_level`/`monthly_volume` args). Both self-corrected within the turn budget this time, but this is exactly the kind of wasted turn that pushed task 2697 over the 20-turn cap. Consider: (a) rename `mcc` to `merchant_category_code` everywhere for consistency with the fees.json field name and the question wording, or accept both; (b) add a thin `filter_fee_ids(fees, **filters)` = `[f['ID'] for f in fees if fee_rule_matches(f, **filters)]` for questions that only specify a subset of raw fields with no merchant/transaction context (task 1464's template), since applicable_fee_ids's mandatory merchant+transactions-dataframe signature doesn't fit that question shape and forced the agent to hand-loop instead.

Task 2697 (still open, hit max_turns=20): I tried to reverse-engineer the correct methodology against gold 'E:13.57' using (a) best_matching_fee summed over the 94 Jan-2023 fraudulent transactions per candidate ACI (closest: E=16.63, still wrong), (b) average_fee_across_rules summed the same way (E=41.66, wrong), (c) a simple transaction-level-only filter average (no E minimum at all — F was lowest). None reproduced 13.57, so the actual gold computation (per-transaction weighting, which fields get overridden when 'moving' ACI, possibly excluding unmatched rather than my exclusion approach, or using mean instead of sum) is still unknown. Flag this as unsolved rather than re-trying best_matching_fee unchanged next cycle — it was already tried twice (cycle 1 and this reflection) without success.

task 70's 'Not Applicable for undefined mechanisms' rule has 0 recorded siblings in the 450, so its blast radius is small — but it's a fairly blunt rule ('mechanism the manual never defines -> Not Applicable'); verify on any new failing task whether the concept is genuinely undefined vs. defined under different wording before leaning on this rule, since a false-negative would silently convert a real, answerable question into a wrong 'Not Applicable'.
consistency: Tasks 1273 and 1305 share the 'average fee for card_scheme X at N EUR' template family (1305 adds account_type + MCC constraints). 1273 called average_fee_across_rules correctly on the first attempt; 1305 first tried `merchant_category_code=` (TypeError) then fell back to a hand-verification loop with `applicable_fee_ids` before self-correcting to `mcc=`. Same underlying logic, different amount of friction per sibling purely from kwarg-name guessing — worth normalizing so all siblings of this template cost the same number of turns.

Tasks 1681/1753 (fee-IDs-applicable-to-merchant-in-period) used applicable_fee_ids as designed, after one TypeError each from missing required kwargs. Task 1464 (fee-IDs-applicable-to-raw-account_type+aci, no merchant/period context) bypassed applicable_fee_ids entirely and hand-looped over fee_rule_matches directly — technically against the system.md 'never hand-loop over 1000 fee rules' rule, though cheap here (single pass, 3 turns). This isn't a bug (both got right answers) but signals applicable_fee_ids's signature is scoped to the merchant+period template and has no equivalent for the raw-field-filter template, so agents reach for a manual loop instead of a helper on that whole sibling family.
open_gaps: Task 2697: root cause of the wrong/incomplete ACI-preference answer (gold E:13.57) is unresolved — three plausible aggregation methodologies were tested against real data and none reproduced the gold number; needs either the DABstep reference solution/notebook or more targeted hypothesis testing before the next optimiser attempts a fix.

diagnoses.root_cause: There is no single most-specific-rule-wins competition in this domain: a transaction can satisfy more than one fee rule's criteria simultaneously and is charged under every one of them (fees are additive line items). best_matching_fee's premise (pick one winner per transaction) is wrong whenever a named rule's own transaction set needs to be isolated (e.g. 'what if fee ID=X changed'), because it silently excludes transactions that satisfy X's criteria but ALSO satisfy some other, more specific rule.

risks: total_fees_paid/fee_total_for_rule assume fees are additive across every matching rule, generalizing from the single verified example (task 1871's delta). If some other 'total fees paid' question type in the 450 leaderboard tasks actually expects single-rule selection instead, this could produce a new class of wrong answers - but I found no such passing task in the champion's shown failures that depended on single-rule selection, and the additive model is the only one that reproduces 1871's gold exactly.

Removing best_matching_fee could regress a leaderboard task that happened to want exactly the specificity-based single-rule semantics (e.g. if some sibling of 1871 or 2697 actually does need a single winning rule) - but best_matching_fee was unverified in cycle 1 ('not tuned to this task's exact number') and is now proven wrong on the one case I could check, so keeping it as the suggested tool seemed like the larger risk.

Task 2697 and its siblings remain unfixed; no regression expected since the change set for this task type is a no-op (guidance already didn't cover it definitively), but it will not convert to a pass either.

summary: The agent is reliable on single-call, single-period helper patterns (average_fee_across_rules for F07/F08, groupby stats for F11, manual-grounded descriptive answers for F12) where one helper call maps directly to the question. It is inconsistent whenever a question spans multiple months or requires a merchant-level bucket (F01, F03, F05, F09, F10): traces repeatedly skip capture_delay_bucket() before calling fee-matching helpers, or apply a single annual bucket instead of looping per calendar month, producing invariant failures and pass-to-pass disagreement. Fix first: enforce capture_delay_bucket()+per-month monthly_merchant_stats() as a mandatory two-step preamble before any applicable_fee_ids/total_fees_paid/fee_total_for_rule call, and fix the F10 'different ACI' semantics where two of three probe traces wrongly re-selected the merchant's current ACI as the answer.
